messages:
Alice M.: Quick intake — bringing up OpenLlama-3b candidate. Main question: which precision stack do we land on (int8, fp8, or gguf) and what's the calibration/gating plan? Goal: ~40% cost reduction vs fp16 while keeping <=2% regression on our core eval set.
Raj K.: Which eval set exactly? conv + code + search?
Alice M.: Yes — convo benchmarks, code generation subset, and semantic-search queries. I attached prompt samples to the PR.
Ben T.: Initial micro-bench on p4d-int8 shows ~30% cost drop, but summarization rouge drops by ~3% on short docs.
Maria S.: Can we try mixed-precision? e.g., int8 for KV/cache, fp16 for attention/dense. Might hit a sweet spot.
Claire L.: Proposal: do a 3-stage sweep: 1) quick smoke (gguf/int8) for correctness, 2) calibration sweep (per-layer scale, group size, clipping), 3) gated canary rollout with metrics.
Ben T.: Note: gguf export path doesn't support fp8 kernels yet. So fp8 path will be a separate runtime experiment.
infra-bot: Deploy job queued — job_id: rwd-deploy-20260316-77abc
Alice M.: Calibration acceptance criteria suggestions: - embedding drift (cosine) <= 0.02 median, - answer accuracy drop <= 1.5% absolute, - rouge/bleu within 2% relative. If any fail, fail the canary.
Raj K.: For embedding drift, add per-task thresholds (search stricter). Also measure recall@10.
Maria S.: For ambiguous generative examples we should include a small human eval slice (30 prompts) to catch quality nuances that metrics miss.
Claire L.: I'll draft a calibration harness: will vary group_size={32,64,128}, clipping={none,0.99,0.95}, symmetric/asymmetric, and per-layer skip list. Output full diffs.
Ben T.: Running a smoke run now: command I used:
```
./run_eval --model openllama-3b --export gguf --quant int8 --tasks conv,code,search --samples 200 --out /tmp/llama_smoke
```
Will post logs.
Raj K.: Canary plan: 5% traffic on dedicated pool for 24h, auto rollback on metric breach. I'll add routing policy: prefer fp8 variant if latency under 1.2x baseline.
Alice M.: Important: include deterministic seed and single-request latency bench (no batching) so we can compare p99 tail.
Ben T.: Uploaded initial smoke logs: s3://redwood-test/llama3b/smoke-1774528912.log — found a determinism flake on code formatting prompts (non-deterministic spacing).
Maria S.: For calibration scoring, use KL divergence on logits distribution + embedding cosine + task-specific accuracy. Weighted score: 0.5 accuracy, 0.3 emb drift, 0.2 KL. Threshold 0.85 pass.
Claire L.: Timeline: today — smoke + triage; tomorrow — full calibration sweep; day after — canary deploy if sweep passes.
Alice M.: Owners: Ben -> gguf/export + smoke artifacts, Raj -> canary routing + SLA config, Maria -> eval harness + human eval slice, Claire -> gating rules + sweep runner.
Ben T.: On it. I'll post per-experiment artifacts and a short README for reproducing.
Alice M.: Thanks team. If sweep shows <1% regression and >30% cost saving we aim to promote. :thumbsup:
Raj K.: Also flag infra quotas — some regions don't have fp8 kernels available. I'll add region gating.
Claire L.: Reminder: include fallback policy: route to fp16 if canary fails or latency > 2x baseline.
Alice M.: Perfect. We'll meet after the calibration run to decide stack. Ping here with results.
